claims.label: Host Says Judge Graf Issued Bindover Ruling After Preliminary Hearing
claims.claim: The host says Judge Graf ruled that the state of Utah met its reliable-hearsay probable-cause standard to bind the case over to trial.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain a certified copy of the bindover order; verify which specific counts were bound over and which were dismissed.

claims.label: Host Says Judge Graf Declined to Dismiss Count 6 (Witness Tampering)
claims.claim: The host says Judge Graf declined to dismiss Count 6 (witness tampering for the "ask for a lawyer and stay silent" text to Lance Twiggs) over the defense's constitutional-rights argument, and she plays a clip of the ruling.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the written ruling; verify the court's exact reasoning and whether a separate written order accompanies the bench ruling.

claims.label: In Ruling Clip Host Plays, Judge Says "Ask for a Lawyer and Stay Silent" Advice Is Lawful Standing Alone
claims.claim: In a clip of the ruling the host plays, the court says that, standing alone, the text "ask for a lawyer and stay silent" describes lawful advice concerning constitutional rights and does not establish witness tampering.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare this on-record concession against the state's preserved theory of the case and any superseding indictment.

claims.label: Host Says Count 5 Is Witness Tampering for the "Delete This Exchange" Message
claims.claim: The host says Count 5 is also witness tampering but pertains strictly to the message in which Tyler Robinson allegedly told Lance Twiggs to "delete this exchange," a separate charge from Count 6.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the charging document to confirm the textual basis alleged for each count.

claims.label: Host Says Judge Tied Count 6 Survival to the Existence of Count 5
claims.claim: The host says the court permitted Count 6 to proceed on the basis of Count 5, and in a clip she plays of the ruling the court says the surrounding communications, including the alleged "delete this exchange" instruction, permit a reasonable inference that the defendant intended Twiggs to withhold information from investigators.
claims.investigative_direction: Determine whether the defense preserved this issue for trial and whether a motion to reconsider or to dismiss post-bindover was filed.

claims.label: In Arraignment Clip Host Plays, Tyler Robinson Pleads Not Guilty to All Counts
claims.claim: In an arraignment clip the host plays, on September 1, 2026, defense counsel enters pleas of not guilty on Tyler Robinson's behalf to all counts in the information.
claims.investigative_direction: Verify against the court's docket entry; track any subsequent plea amendments.

claims.label: In Arraignment Clip Host Plays, Defense Waives Reading of the Information
claims.claim: In an arraignment clip the host plays, defense counsel says he waives reading of the information before entering not-guilty pleas.
claims.investigative_direction: Confirm docket entry; verify whether this waiver affects any future challenge to the sufficiency of the information.

claims.label: Justin Davis sprinted to and opened the passenger door of a vehicle he did not arrive in
claims.claim: The host says that in footage she shows of the post-shot sequence, Justin Davis (driver of the Lincoln Navigator) sprinted to and opened the passenger-side door of a vehicle he had not arrived in, alongside Blake Neff, who was also not a passenger of that vehicle.
claims.investigative_direction: Cross-reference vehicle key logs, security team statements, and any post-event interviews with Davis and Neff to confirm.

claims.label: Host Says Mikey McCoy and Danny Philip Met in a Coordinated Manner at Kirk's Vehicle
claims.claim: The host says footage she shows has Mikey McCoy and Danny Philip running, meeting, and "ducking down" together with Justin Davis in front of Kirk's vehicle, in what she characterizes as a coordinated sequence.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain original footage for frame-by-frame analysis; obtain statements from McCoy and Phillip regarding this movement.

claims.label: Host Says Mikey McCoy's Hand Remained at His Ear Throughout the Post-Shot Sequence
claims.claim: The host says that throughout the run to and at Kirk's vehicle, Mikey McCoy kept his hand at his ear, which she says she has been told repeatedly was only to cover noise rather than a phone call.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare frame-by-frame footage against cell-phone metadata / call detail records; obtain McCoy's own account.

claims.label: A backpack was ejected from the trunk of Kirk's vehicle
claims.claim: The host says that as Kirk's vehicle departed for the hospital, a backpack fell or was tossed from the trunk; she thinks it is "Chris's bag" but says she is "not 100% certain."
claims.investigative_direction: Identify the bag's owner; obtain receipt / loss-property reports if any.

claims.label: Kirk communicated the night before 9/10 that he feared for his life
claims.claim: The host says we now know for a fact that Charlie Kirk communicated the night before that he was fearful for his life and thought they were going to kill him, something she says his wife Erika Kirk initially denied and then had to concede, and that people are now saying he also told his security people to be on him and no one else.
claims.investigative_direction: Locate the original source(s) of the prior-night fear claim and corroborate against contemporaneous records (texts, voice mails, third-party accounts).

claims.label: Host Says Christopher and Nate Walker Were Upstairs Near the Sorensen Building Minutes Before the Shot
claims.claim: The host says Christopher (Kirk's main security person) and Nate Walker walked toward the Sorensen building and were upstairs in the minutes before the shot, in a clip she thinks was captured on TikTok and sent to Baron Coleman.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain original TikTok source footage with timestamp; obtain statements from Christopher and Walker regarding their location and purpose.

claims.label: Host Says Christopher's Absence From the Vehicle Preceded the Shot by Minutes
claims.claim: The host says Christopher left the immediate vehicle area and went upstairs minutes before the shot, and that by the time he came back downstairs, his car was gone.
claims.investigative_direction: Cross-reference against security radio logs and Christopher's own timeline.

claims.label: Host Says Sources Told Her Three Security Vehicles Were Not Driven to the Hospital
claims.claim: The host says, citing "sources with direct knowledge," that Danny Philip and Blake Neff's Denali was not driven to the hospital, and says that all three security vehicles (the lead Jeep Wagoneer, the Lincoln Navigator, and the second Yukon Denali) were left behind.
claims.investigative_direction: Identify the named sources; cross-reference against vehicle GPS / fleet logs and security team statements.

claims.label: Host Says UVU Security Vehicles Arrived Between 9:00 and 9:30 a.m. on 9/10
claims.claim: The host says that, based on the security team's testimonies, the two security vehicles (a black Jeep Wagoneer and a Lincoln Navigator) arrived at UVU between 9:00 and 9:30 a.m., independently of Charlie Kirk, while he was at the restaurantology event in Salt Lake City.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain toll/transponder logs, security radio logs, or vehicle GPS records to verify arrival times.

claims.label: Two security team members remain unidentified
claims.claim: Two members of the Charlie Kirk security team shown in the security photo remain unidentified by the host: one in a short-sleeve bright blue shirt at front-right, and one in a hat with a beard in the middle.
claims.investigative_direction: Cross-reference with TPUSA-published security team rosters, event staffing contracts, and 9/10 security team statements.

claims.label: Matt Walsh X post characterized defense counsel as justifying political assassination
claims.claim: On September 1, 2026, Matt Walsh posted on X: "We have a lawyer justifying political assassination in one court case, and another lawyer justifying the mass murder of children in another. Very dark times in America."
claims.investigative_direction: Confirm the post remains on X; verify timestamp; cross-reference Walsh's full thread for context.

claims.label: Host Rejects Walsh's Framing of the Defense Argument
claims.claim: The host explicitly rejects Walsh's "justifying political assassination" framing and characterizes it as a "disingenuous narrative."
claims.investigative_direction: This is a host-stance claim; verification would require Walsh's reply or retraction.

claims.label: Viva Frei echoed the same political-assassination framing

claims.investigative_direction: Locate the specific post; verify timestamp.

claims.label: Graham Allen X post accused defense counsel of attacking Charlie Kirk in court
claims.claim: Graham Allen posted on X: "Are you kidding me? Are you kidding me? Tyler Robinson's defense attorney attacked Charlie Kirk in court. This man is a lunatic."
claims.investigative_direction: Confirm the post remains on X; verify timestamp.

claims.label: Blake Neff and Brandon Tatum sent an identical X post about Novak
claims.claim: Blake Neff and Brandon Tatum sent an identical X post accusing defense attorney Richard Novak of "trashing Charlie" by stating that Kirk "spoke hatefully about people who were not heterosexual or had sex outside of marriage."
claims.investigative_direction: Confirm both posts remain on X; compare timestamps.

claims.label: Host Says Defense Counsel Framed His Argument as a Citation of the State's Own Theory
claims.claim: The host says defense counsel Richard Novak, in his probable-cause-hearing argument, was not advancing a personal thesis that political assassinations are acceptable but was citing the state's own theory to argue that the state had failed to satisfy its burden even on its own framing.
claims.investigative_direction: Read Novak's full argument transcript; compare against Aug 11 filing page 32 and the state's responsive briefing.

claims.label: Host Says State Is Pursuing Sentence Enhancement Based on Political Motivation
claims.claim: The host says the state is pursuing sentence enhancements on the theory that Charlie Kirk was targeted for his political or religious beliefs, with the "some hate just can't be negotiated" text as the central anchor.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the state's sentencing-enhancement motion and the controlling Utah statute to verify the elements and the state's proffer.

claims.label: Host Says State Has Not Identified Specific Kirk Statements Alleged to Be "Hateful"
claims.claim: The host says Tyler Robinson's lawyer is arguing that the state's filings do not identify which specific statements by Charlie Kirk they contend are "hateful" toward the LGBTQ community, and that the state is inferring upon an inference.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the state's filing in full; enumerate the specific statements cited; compare against defense's enumeration.

claims.label: Defense page 32 asserts inference-upon-inference as to political motivation
claims.claim: Per the August 11 defense filing the host shows (page 32), "There's no evidence of specific political expressions of Mr. Kirk which, if any, Mr. Robinson may have been aware of or focused on"; the host says the defense argues the state is "inferring upon an inference."
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain page 32 directly; compare with the state's response and the preliminary-hearing transcript.

claims.label: Per Defense Filing Host Reads, State's Theory Turns in Part on Twiggs's Intermittent Non-Gender-Conforming Identification
claims.claim: Per the defense filing the host shows and reads (page 32), the state's theory relies in part on the proposition that Lance Twiggs, and not Tyler Robinson, was "at least intermittently identifying as a female to his close friends," as part of the inferential chain supporting the political-motivation enhancement.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the state's proffer; obtain any statements or records from Twiggs or third parties regarding gender identification.

claims.label: Blake Neff's testimony describes a 20-second window from "active shooter" to "all clear"
claims.claim: Blake Neff testified that after the shot he and Mikey McCoy ran because they believed there might be more shooters, but that approximately 15–20 seconds later he concluded the shooter had likely been "detained or stopped" and that they were not in immediate danger.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the full transcript of Neff's testimony; cross-reference against contemporaneous radio traffic and other security personnel.

claims.label: Blake Neff testified that Mikey McCoy called "Erika" from the scene
claims.claim: Blake Neff testified that Mikey McCoy, within approximately one minute of the shot, called "Erika" (Erica / Erika Kirk) and then called his father Rob McCoy.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain Erika Kirk's call detail records; verify call timing and duration.

claims.label: "Mikey said there's so much blood" claim traces to Hibbs / Turek, not McCoy
claims.claim: The host says the "so much blood" claim attributed to Mikey McCoy did not originate with McCoy himself; she says it came from his father, from Jack Hibbs and, she thinks, Frank Turek, i.e. "the pastor orbit," and that McCoy never described seeing a lot of blood in his press.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain McCoy's complete media appearances; obtain Hibbs's and Turek's on-record statements with timestamps; obtain Erika Kirk's call-detail records (the call McCoy made to her per Neff testimony).

claims.label: Brian Harpole stated there were no threats the night before 9/10
claims.claim: The host says Brian Harpole, sitting down with Shawn Ryan, said there were no threats the night before September 10, which she presents as in tension with Kirk's prior-night communication of fear.
claims.investigative_direction: Locate the Shawn Ryan interview clip; obtain Harpole's full statement; cross-reference against Kirk's prior-night communications.
